newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil government says reducing federal costs.
newsitem.headline: Brazil government says reducing federal costs.

text.p: The Brazilian federal government is succeeding in reducing monthly payroll and social security costs and expects to stabilize expenditure over the coming months, the Finance Ministry said Thursday.
The ministry said in its monthly report on economic indicators that the federal government managed to cut expenditure in August by 2.4 percent over July, mainly due to lower payroll costs.
It added the federal government expected its payroll to "stabilize" at about 3.0 billion reais per month, an amount "slightly lower than the average since September 1995".
In August, federal payroll costs totalled 2.9 billion reais.
The ministry's monthly report on economic indicators, introduced some four months ago, does not necessarily reflect "official" views, being based on independent market forecasts.

The federal government's primary surplus in the first eight months of the year stood at 0.66 percent of gross domestic product, an improvement on the 0.52 percent primary surplus registered in the same year-ago period, it said.
The federal government's operational deficit was 1.26 percent of GDP versus 1.79 percent in the January to August period 1995.

"It can be observed that the main contributor to the result was a reduction in expenditure," the ministry said. "In global terms, the spending of the federal government showed a decrease of 0.54 percent of GDP."
